title: About the non-random Content of Financial Markets

extraction.methodology_summary: The paper designs a trend-following trading strategy using high-frequency (5-minute) data. The strategy uses four exponential moving averages of different lengths, with crossings acting as potential trade triggers conditioned on volatility ranges and specific exit rules. The model is optimized on an in-sample period, validated on an out-of-sample period, and tested on a live-sample period, alongside extensive stress testing.
extraction.universe: Euro future contract (EC), DAX future (FDAX), and Cacao future (CC)

key_findings: Financial markets exhibit small but detectable non-random, trend-following behavior when analyzed using multivariate statistical methods.
A trend-following strategy conditioned on volatility ranges and exit thresholds can generate consistent profits (net of fees) across different market regimes.
The trading system is robust against data randomization and various stress tests (e.g., delayed execution, increased fees).
The identified trend-following invariants are transferable across largely uncorrelated assets, such as the Euro future, DAX future, and Cacao future.
limitations: The authors note that this is not a general proof of statistical inference, as they focus on specific examples and generality cannot be claimed.
The rationale behind the parameters and herding behaviors is complex and not fully explained.
